scope: AQA Physics AS mock: six required practical activities
notes: Original RP1–RP6 coverage plus applied AS Paper 2 practical, graph, uncertainty and cross-topic problem-solving. Model answers reviewed and no existing IDs replaced.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: rp1
questions.prompt: A vibrating string of length 0.80 m shows four stationary-wave loops at 30 Hz. Mass per metre is 0.015 kg m⁻¹. Find the wavelength, wave speed and string tension; explain why the string length is controlled. [6 marks]
markPoints: Four loops correspond to four half-wavelengths.
Keeping length constant isolates the effect of varying tension.
questions.modelAnswer: λ=0.40 m; v=12 m s⁻¹; T=2.16 N using T=μv². Keep string length fixed to isolate the independent variable.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: rp2
questions.prompt: A diffraction grating has 500 lines per millimetre. A first-order maximum is observed at 22.0°. Calculate the grating spacing and wavelength. Explain why corresponding angles on both sides should be measured. [6 marks]
markPoints: Measuring corresponding angles on both sides and averaging reduces alignment error.
questions.modelAnswer: d=2.00×10⁻⁶ m. At order n=1, λ=d sin22.0°=7.49×10⁻⁷ m (749 nm). Average corresponding angles measured on either side.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: rp3
questions.prompt: A steel ball is released from rest and travels 0.800 m in 0.405 s. Calculate g; explain how the gradient of a displacement against time-squared graph relates to g; identify one timing improvement. [6 marks]
markPoints: Use s=½gt² for release from rest.
Graph displacement s vertically against t² horizontally.
Gradient=g/2, so g is twice the gradient.
Electronic timing reduces human reaction-time uncertainty.
questions.modelAnswer: g=2×0.800/0.405²=9.75 m s⁻². Plot s against t²: gradient=g/2. Electronic timing improves precision.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: rp4
questions.prompt: A 2.00 m elastic wire has diameter 0.500 mm. A force of 10.0 N increases its length by 0.500 mm. Calculate cross-sectional area and Young modulus; explain why a longer wire helps. [6 marks]
markPoints: A longer wire gives larger measurable extension, reducing relative uncertainty.
questions.modelAnswer: A=π(5.00×10⁻⁴)²/4=1.963×10⁻⁷ m². E=10.0×2.00/(A×5.00×10⁻⁴)=2.04×10¹¹ Pa. A longer wire yields a more measurable extension.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: rp5
questions.prompt: A conducting wire has length 1.50 m, diameter 0.300 mm and resistance 4.00 Ω. Calculate resistivity. Explain how 2.0% uncertainty in diameter affects the area uncertainty and why heating is undesirable. [6 marks]
markPoints: Area A=πd²/4 with d in metres.
As A∝d², diameter uncertainty gives about 4.0% uncertainty in area.
Heating changes the resistance and resistivity, compromising a fair measurement.
questions.modelAnswer: A=7.07×10⁻⁸ m². ρ=4.00A/1.50=1.88×10⁻⁷ Ω m. Area uncertainty≈4%; avoid heating because resistance depends on temperature.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: rp6
questions.prompt: A cell produces three (I, V) readings: (0.10 A,1.45 V), (0.20 A,1.40 V), (0.30 A,1.35 V). Determine the gradient, internal resistance and emf; explain why terminal voltage falls as current rises. [6 marks]
markPoints: r is the magnitude of the negative gradient: 0.50 Ω.
The internal lost volts Ir increase with current, reducing terminal voltage.
questions.modelAnswer: Gradient=−0.50 Ω; from V=ε−Ir, r=0.50 Ω and ε=1.50 V. As current rises, Ir increases and terminal p.d. falls.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: data01
questions.prompt: A force–extension graph has a best-fit gradient of 0.250 N mm⁻¹. Acceptable steepest and shallowest gradients are 0.267 and 0.233 N mm⁻¹. Convert the best-fit gradient to N m⁻¹, calculate its absolute and percentage uncertainty, and explain why a best-fit line is used. [6 marks]
markPoints: Recognise that the best-fit gradient is 0.250 N mm⁻¹.
Convert by 1000 to obtain 250 N m⁻¹.
Absolute gradient uncertainty = (0.267−0.233)/2 = 0.017 N mm⁻¹ (17 N m⁻¹).
A best-fit line represents the data trend despite random scatter; use extreme lines consistent with uncertainty bars.
questions.modelAnswer: Best-fit gradient 0.250 N mm⁻¹ = 250 N m⁻¹. Uncertainty = (0.267−0.233)/2 = 0.017 N mm⁻¹ = 17 N m⁻¹, or 6.8%. A best-fit line reduces the effect of scattered readings.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: data02
questions.prompt: A micrometer reads +0.050 mm when its jaws are fully closed. The displayed diameter of a wire is 0.500 mm. Find the corrected diameter and cross-sectional area. Explain the type of error and why simply repeating readings would not remove it. [6 marks]
markPoints: A non-zero reading at closure indicates a systematic zero error.
Subtract the +0.050 mm offset: corrected d = 0.450 mm.
Use A = πd²/4 (diameter, not radius, in the formula).
Repeated readings alone cannot eliminate a systematic offset; zero-correct/calibrate the micrometer.
questions.modelAnswer: The +0.050 mm zero error is systematic, so d = 0.500−0.050 = 0.450 mm = 4.50×10⁻⁴ m. A = πd²/4 = 1.59×10⁻⁷ m². Repeating does not cancel a fixed zero error.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: data03
questions.prompt: Resistivity is calculated from ρ = Rπd²/(4L). Measurements are R = (10.0 ± 0.2) Ω, d = (0.500 ± 0.010) mm and L = (1.50 ± 0.01) m. Estimate the percentage uncertainty in ρ, showing every contribution. [6 marks]
markPoints: Because d is squared, its contribution is 2×2.0% = 4.0%.
For a product/quotient, add percentage uncertainty contributions.
questions.modelAnswer: ρ = Rπd²/(4L): % uncertainty ≈ %R+2(%d)+%L = 2.0+4.0+0.67 = 6.67%, approximately 6.7%. The factor 2 comes from the squared diameter.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: data04
questions.prompt: A photoelectric experiment gives stopping potentials of 0.40 V at frequency 6.0×10¹⁴ Hz and 1.23 V at 8.0×10¹⁴ Hz. Calculate the gradient of stopping potential against frequency, use it to estimate Planck's constant (e = 1.60×10⁻¹⁹ C), and estimate threshold frequency. [6 marks]
markPoints: Change in stopping potential is 1.23−0.40 = 0.83 V.
From eVₛ = hf−φ, stopping-potential gradient = h/e.
Extrapolating Vₛ to zero gives f₀ = 6.0×10¹⁴−0.40/(4.15×10⁻¹⁵) ≈ 5.04×10¹⁴ Hz.
questions.modelAnswer: Gradient = 0.83/(2.0×10¹⁴) = 4.15×10⁻¹⁵ V Hz⁻¹. Since Vₛ = (h/e)f−φ/e, h = 6.64×10⁻³⁴ J s. The x-intercept gives f₀ ≈ 5.04×10¹⁴ Hz.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: data05
questions.prompt: In a Young's double-slit experiment the measured fringe spacing is 2.40 mm at screen distance 0.80 m, and 3.60 mm at 1.20 m. Slit separation is 0.200 mm. Find the gradient of fringe spacing against screen distance, calculate wavelength, and explain one method of reducing percentage uncertainty in fringe spacing. [6 marks]
markPoints: Convert fringe spacings to 0.00240 m and 0.00360 m.
Therefore the w-against-D gradient equals λ/a.
Measure the distance across several fringes and divide by the number of fringe spacings, reducing relative uncertainty.
questions.modelAnswer: Gradient of w against D = 0.00120/0.40 = 0.00300. From w = λD/a, λ = gradient×a = 0.00300×2.00×10⁻⁴ = 6.00×10⁻⁷ m. Measure across many fringes to reduce % uncertainty.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: data06
questions.prompt: An LDR and a fixed 2.0 kΩ resistor are connected in series across a 6.0 V supply; voltage is measured across the fixed resistor. The LDR is 4.0 kΩ in dim light and 1.0 kΩ in bright light. Calculate both output voltages, explain their change and state one variable to control for a fair comparison. [6 marks]
markPoints: Identify the fixed resistor and LDR as series components; output voltage is across the fixed resistor.
Greater illumination lowers LDR resistance, raising the fraction of the supply across the fixed resistor.
Keep supply voltage constant when changing illumination (or control other background light).
questions.modelAnswer: With output across the fixed resistor, Vout = 6.0×2.0/(2.0+RLDR) using kΩ. Dim: 2.0 V; bright: 4.0 V. More light lowers LDR resistance, so output rises. Keep supply voltage fixed.
